done.what: Remove the sofa: the rug under it is no longer a pale tiled patch with a seam and a step. New engine/mend.ts `weaveFill`: the rug is unwarped onto its plane (samples `plane`, its four corners), its weave (photo over its own colour close by) is quilted into the hidden part (Efros–Freeman blocks, best match of what shows, cheapest-path seams, rows processed from the side the rug shows on), laid back through the plane from the photo's own pixels at full sharpness, in the rug's colour at the same depth (each row's lighter half where it shows clear). The rug next to the throw is lifted out of the sofa's shade (sofa `casts`) and eased into the laid part; a 10 px band is quilted and faded so no straight join remains; the rug's front and left edges get the thin dark line its visible edges have. A sliver (a fig's saucer brushing the rug's corner) is left as photographed.

Remove the sofa: the armchair is rebuilt part by part instead of mirrored (new generic `rebuild` steps on a sample piece: rows / columns / along / copy / shade): the shade under its seat, its seat top and front on from the end that shows, its left arm post down to the floor, its side beside the post, its back leg copied from the post — no white arm block, seat blob, white wedges, leg stub, or seat wider than its back. The sofa's cut was retraced round the pillows (the post and the seat top are the chair's again). A step can be `frame`: after a sofa Remove, a Replace/Customize of the chair paints the rebuilt upholstery but never the wooden post and leg.

Remove the sofa: the coffee table stands on four legs (front and back left legs copied from the right front leg), the space under its top in shade, its top's front edge and the rail under it continued along the edge where the throw hid them (the `along` step averages the first stretch that shows at the pixel's exact offset across the line — straight and crisp, no streaks or steps); the table's cut now stops where the sofa's back starts (no light sofa rim left under the top).

Remove the coffee table: the TV console's hidden base is rebuilt — drawer fronts down their columns (a couple of pixels past the bowl's rim, so no pale lines), the light edge / shadow gap / dark under it along its length, and its missing left leg copied from the right one — no torn stair-stepped rail, no white gap line, no floating end; the rug where the table and its leg stood is laid by the weave (no slab).

Remove the rug: no dark rug wedge by the throw — the sofa's cut follows the throw and its fringe, and a new `wisps` zone keys the fringe against what is behind it (only the light strands stay; the floor shows between them).

Remove the armchair: it takes its soft shade on the wall and the floor (a traced `plate`), so no grey ghost stays on the wall; the floor lamp's pole runs on from below its shade (no pale stub); the right curtain's folds run on down to the hem behind the chair and the sofa's cushions (never the plate's differently-lit curtain in blocks).

Remove the sofa: no dark smudge of its shade on the floor in front of it (its plate now reaches the picture's foot, so the light match reads the floor clear of the shade); every Remove takes the piece's rim (2 px past its outline) even where a traced plate runs along the cut; rebuilt edge pixels count in full (two areas traced edge to edge leave no half-done pixel).

Deterministic (a second render is byte-identical).

Engine: a Generate with a Remove lifts the pieces once and starts every variant from that picture (3 variants no longer pay the lift three times); rugs are mended before the pieces standing on them.
